recipes.title: Egusi Soup

benefits: High in healthy fats from palm oil
Egusi seeds are rich in protein and omega-3
Leafy greens provide iron and vitamins
risks: Palm oil is high in saturated fat — consume in moderation

instructions: Step 1: Blend the egusi seeds into a fine powder.
Step 2: Heat palm oil in a pot and add chopped onions; sauté until translucent.
Step 3: Stir in the blended egusi and fry for a few minutes.
Step 4: Add water gradually, stirring to avoid lumps, and let it simmer.
Step 5: Add the spinach, pepper, and salt; cook for an additional 10 minutes.

recipes.title: Jollof Rice

benefits: Bell peppers are rich in vitamin C
risks: High in carbohydrates — watch portion size if diabetic
Can be high in sodium from seasoning cubes

instructions: Step 1: In a pot, sauté chopped onions until golden.
Step 2: Add blended tomatoes and bell peppers; cook until reduced.
Step 3: Stir in thyme, curry powder, salt, and pepper.
Step 4: Add rice and mix well with the sauce.
Step 5: Pour in the broth, cover, and simmer on low heat until rice is cooked.

recipes.title: Gari Fortor

benefits: Beans provide plant protein and fiber
risks: Processed gari is low in micronutrients

instructions: Step 1: In a pan, heat palm oil and sauté chopped onions until soft.
Step 2: Add cooked beans and stir for a few minutes.
Step 3: Gradually add gari while mixing until well combined.
Step 4: Season with salt and serve warm.

recipes.title: Gari with Pepper Soup

benefits: Pepper soup spices may have anti-inflammatory properties
risks: Very spicy — avoid if sensitive to heat

instructions: Step 1: In a pot, bring chicken or fish stock to a boil.
Step 2: Add sliced onions and pepper soup spice mix; simmer for 10 minutes.
Step 3: Gradually sprinkle gari into the pot while stirring.
Step 4: Cook until thickened, then season with salt and serve hot.

recipes.title: Gari and Groundnut

benefits: Groundnuts are rich in healthy fats and protein
risks: Added sugar may spike blood glucose

instructions: Step 1: In a bowl, mix gari and groundnuts.
Step 2: Add sugar or honey to taste.
Step 3: Pour water or milk over the mixture and stir until combined.
Step 4: Let it sit for a few minutes to soften before serving.

recipes.title: Gari and Fish Stew

risks: Fried fish may be high in oil

ingredients: 2 cups fish (cleaned and cut into pieces)
instructions: Step 1: In a pot, sauté chopped onions until golden.
Step 2: Add fish pieces and cook until lightly browned.
Step 3: Stir in tomato sauce, salt, and pepper; simmer for 10 minutes.
Step 4: Prepare gari by soaking it in hot water.
Step 5: Serve the fish stew over the gari.

recipes.title: Gari with Milk

benefits: Milk provides calcium and vitamin D
risks: Low in protein compared to main meals

instructions: Step 1: In a bowl, mix gari with sugar.
Step 2: Pour milk over the gari and stir to combine.
Step 3: Add a sprinkle of cinnamon if desired.
Step 4: Let it sit for a few minutes before serving.

recipes.title: Bitterleaf Soup

benefits: Bitterleaf is rich in vitamins and antioxidants
Groundnut paste provides protein and healthy fats
risks: High in calories if eaten in large quantities

instructions: Step 1: Rinse and squeeze bitterleaf to reduce bitterness.
Step 2: In a pot, sauté onions until translucent.
Step 3: Add meat or fish and cook until tender.
Step 4: Stir in groundnut paste, salt, and seasoning cubes.
Step 5: Add water to achieve desired consistency, and simmer for 20 minutes.

recipes.title: Nkwobi

benefits: High collagen from cow foot — supports joint health
Crayfish is rich in protein and minerals
Palm oil has vitamin A and E

instructions: Step 1: In a pot, heat palm oil and sauté chopped onions.
Step 2: Add cooked cow foot and stir to combine.
Step 3: Mix in ground crayfish, pepper, and salt; simmer for 10 minutes.
Step 4: Serve in a bowl, often garnished with sliced onions.

recipes.title: Ofada Rice and Ayamase

benefits: Ofada rice is unpolished and high in fiber
Assorted meat provides protein and iron
Green peppers are rich in vitamin C
risks: Palm oil is high in saturated fat

instructions: Step 1: Rinse and cook Ofada rice in boiling water until soft.
Step 2: Blend green peppers and onion into a smooth paste.
Step 3: In a pot, heat palm oil and add the blended mixture; cook for 10 minutes.
Step 4: Add assorted meat, salt, and seasoning; simmer for another 10 minutes.
Step 5: Serve the sauce over cooked Ofada rice.

recipes.title: Pounded Yam and Egusi Soup

benefits: Yam is a good source of potassium and vitamin C

instructions: Step 1: Boil yam until soft, then pound until smooth.
Step 2: Blend egusi seeds into a fine powder.
Step 3: Heat palm oil, add onions, and sauté until translucent.
Step 4: Stir in blended egusi, and cook for a few minutes.
Step 5: Gradually add water and simmer until thickened; serve with pounded yam.

recipes.title: Okra Soup

benefits: Okra is high in soluble fiber — good for digestion
Rich in vitamin K and folate
risks: Okra can reduce absorption of some medicines — space out medication

instructions: Step 1: In a pot, heat palm oil and sauté onions until soft.
Step 2: Add meat or fish and cook until tender.
Step 3: Stir in sliced okra and cook for 10 minutes.
Step 4: Season with salt and seasoning; serve hot.

recipes.title: Moi Moi

benefits: Black-eyed peas are high in protein and fiber
risks: Some recipes add a lot of palm oil — check portion
May be high in sodium if over-seasoned

instructions: Step 1: Blend soaked black-eyed peas, onion, and bell pepper into a smooth paste.
Step 2: Stir in palm oil, salt, and seasoning.
Step 3: Pour the mixture into leaves or bowls.
Step 4: Steam for about 45 minutes until firm.
Step 5: Serve warm as a side dish or snack.

recipes.title: Peppered Chicken

benefits: High protein — great for muscle repair
Pepper has capsaicin which may boost metabolism
risks: Fried in palm oil — high saturated fat

instructions: Step 1: Marinate chicken with salt, pepper sauce, and chopped onions for at least 30 minutes.
Step 2: In a pot, heat palm oil and fry the marinated chicken until golden.
Step 3: Add more chopped onions and simmer for 10-15 minutes.
Step 4: Adjust seasoning if necessary and serve hot.

recipes.title: Efo Riro

benefits: Spinach is packed with iron and vitamins A, C, K
risks: High in fat from palm oil
Spinach can reduce calcium absorption if eaten in huge amounts

instructions: Step 1: In a pot, heat palm oil and sauté onions until soft.
Step 2: Add blended bell pepper and cook for 10 minutes.
Step 3: Stir in chopped spinach and cook until wilted.
Step 4: Season with salt and seasoning; serve hot.

recipes.title: Akara

risks: High in calories if eaten in large quantities

instructions: Step 1: Blend soaked black-eyed peas with onion and peppers.
Step 2: Pour the mixture into a bowl and season with salt.
Step 3: Heat oil in a frying pan.
Step 4: Scoop the mixture and fry until golden brown on both sides.
Step 5: Serve warm as a snack or breakfast.

recipes.title: Catfish Pepper Soup

benefits: Warming and hydrating — traditionally eaten when sick

instructions: Step 1: In a pot, add sliced onions and water; bring to a boil.
Step 2: Add catfish and pepper soup spice; simmer for 20 minutes.
Step 3: Season with salt and adjust spice to taste.
Step 4: Serve hot with sides.

recipes.title: Banga Soup

benefits: Palm nut extract is rich in vitamin A and E
Assorted meats provide protein and iron

instructions: Step 1: Boil palm nuts in water, then extract the oil.
Step 2: In a pot, sauté onions and assorted meats until tender.
Step 3: Stir in extracted palm oil and banga spice; simmer for 20 minutes.
Step 4: Serve with rice or starch.

recipes.title: Plantain Fufu

benefits: Rich in potassium and vitamin B6
risks: High in carbs — not ideal for diabetics in large amounts

instructions: Step 1: Boil peeled plantains until soft.
Step 2: Drain and mash until smooth and stretchy.
Step 3: Serve warm with soups or stews.

recipes.title: Beans and Plantain Porridge
instructions: Step 1: Boil beans in water until tender.
Step 2: Add sliced plantains and chopped onions; cook until plantains are soft.
Step 3: Season with salt and stir to combine.
Step 4: Serve warm.

recipes.title: Ewedu Soup

benefits: Ewedu leaves are high in vitamin A, C, and iron

instructions: Step 1: Wash ewedu leaves thoroughly.
Step 2: In a pot, add ewedu leaves and cook with a little water until soft.
Step 3: Stir in ground crayfish, palm oil, salt, and seasoning; simmer for 10 minutes.
Step 4: Serve with pounded yam or rice.

recipes.title: Nigerian Salad

benefits: Fresh vegetables provide vitamins and minerals
risks: Mayonnaise is high in fat and calories

instructions: Step 1: In a large bowl, mix cooked macaroni and vegetables.
Step 2: Stir in chopped onions and mayonnaise.
Step 3: Top with sliced boiled eggs.
Step 4: Serve chilled or at room temperature.

recipes.title: Efo Elegusi

benefits: Combines protein-rich egusi with iron-rich spinach

instructions: Step 1: Blend egusi seeds into a powder.
Step 2: In a pot, heat palm oil and sauté onions.
Step 3: Add blended egusi and stir-fry for 5 minutes.
Step 4: Add chopped spinach, salt, and pepper; simmer until spinach wilts.

recipes.title: Kelewele
instructions: Step 1: In a bowl, mix sliced plantains with ginger, cayenne pepper, and salt.
Step 2: Heat oil in a frying pan.
Step 3: Fry plantain slices until golden brown.
Step 4: Serve hot as a snack or side dish.

recipes.title: Peppered Fish
instructions: Step 1: Marinate fish with salt and pepper sauce for at least 30 minutes.
Step 2: In a frying pan, heat oil and fry the fish until golden brown.
Step 3: Add sliced onions and stir-fry for a few minutes.
Step 4: Serve hot with sides.

recipes.title: Ofada Rice and Ayamase Sauce

benefits: Ofada rice is high fiber and unpolished
Green peppers are rich in vitamin C

instructions: Step 1: Cook ofada rice until soft and fluffy.
Step 2: Blend green bell peppers, scotch bonnet, and onions into a smooth paste.
Step 3: In a pot, cook assorted meats until tender.
Step 4: Add the blended paste to the pot, stir and simmer for 15 minutes.
Step 5: Serve the sauce over the rice.

recipes.title: Peppered Snails

benefits: Snails are very high in protein and low in fat
Low calorie for a protein source
risks: Must be cleaned and cooked thoroughly — risk of parasites if undercooked

instructions: Step 1: In a pot, boil snails until tender.
Step 2: In a frying pan, heat oil and fry sliced onions until golden.
Step 3: Add boiled snails and pepper sauce, stir-fry for 5-7 minutes.
Step 4: Serve hot as a snack.

recipes.title: Coconut Rice

risks: High in saturated fat from coconut

instructions: Step 1: In a pot, sauté chopped onions until soft.
Step 2: Add bell peppers and cook for a few minutes.
Step 3: Stir in rice, coconut milk, and salt; cook until rice is tender.
Step 4: Serve hot as a side dish.

recipes.title: Ofe Nsala (White Soup)
instructions: Step 1: In a pot, boil chicken or goat meat with onions until tender.
Step 2: Add ground crayfish and salt, and simmer for 10 minutes.
Step 3: Serve hot as a soup.

recipes.title: Nkwobi (Cow Foot Dish)

benefits: Cow foot is rich in collagen — good for joints and skin

instructions: Step 1: In a bowl, combine boiled cow foot with onions, potash, and pepper.
Step 2: Mix in palm oil to achieve a desired consistency.
Step 3: Serve warm, garnished with sliced onions.

recipes.title: Peppered Goat Meat

benefits: Goat meat is leaner than beef

instructions: Step 1: Marinate goat meat with salt and pepper sauce for at least 30 minutes.
Step 2: In a frying pan, heat oil and fry goat meat until golden brown.
Step 3: Add chopped onions and stir-fry for a few minutes.
Step 4: Serve hot as a snack or main dish.

recipes.title: Jollof Spaghetti

benefits: Can add vegetables for more nutrients

instructions: Step 1: Cook spaghetti in boiling water until al dente; drain.
Step 2: In a pot, sauté onions until golden.
Step 3: Add blended tomatoes and tomato paste; cook for 10 minutes.
Step 4: Stir in cooked spaghetti and spices; serve hot.

recipes.title: Chin Chin
instructions: Step 1: In a bowl, mix flour, sugar, baking powder, and milk to form a dough.
Step 2: Roll out the dough and cut into small pieces.
Step 3: In a frying pan, heat oil and fry chin chin until golden brown.
Step 4: Drain on paper towels and serve as a snack.

recipes.title: Fish Pepper Soup
instructions: Step 1: In a pot, boil fish with onions and pepper sauce until cooked.
Step 2: Add seasoning and adjust water to desired consistency.
Step 3: Serve hot as a soup.

recipes.title: Fried Rice

benefits: Carrots and peas add vitamins and fiber
risks: Can be high in sodium from seasoning

instructions: Step 1: Cook rice and set aside.
Step 2: In a pan, sauté onions and carrots until soft.
Step 3: Add cooked rice and mix well with spices.
Step 4: Serve hot as a side dish.

recipes.title: Suya

benefits: Spices like ginger and paprika have antioxidants
risks: Grilled meat — charred parts may contain carcinogens

instructions: Step 1: Mix suya spice with oil to form a paste.
Step 2: Coat beef slices with the spice paste.
Step 3: Skewer the meat.
Step 4: Grill over high heat, turning often, until charred and cooked through.
Step 5: Serve with sliced onions and tomatoes.

recipes.title: Puff Puff
instructions: Step 1: Mix flour, sugar, yeast, and water into a smooth batter.
Step 2: Cover and let rise 1 hour.
Step 3: Heat oil in a deep pan.
Step 4: Scoop batter balls into oil; fry until golden.
Step 5: Drain and serve warm.

recipes.title: Asaro (Yam Porridge)

benefits: Yam is rich in potassium and vitamin C

instructions: Step 1: Boil yam until halfway tender.
Step 2: Add blended tomatoes, onions, and palm oil.
Step 3: Simmer until yam is soft and sauce thickens.
Step 4: Stir in spinach; cook 3 more minutes.
Step 5: Season and serve warm.

recipes.title: Ewa Agoyin

benefits: Beans are an excellent source of plant protein
risks: Sauce is high in palm oil

instructions: Step 1: Boil beans until very soft; mash slightly.
Step 2: Heat palm oil and fry onions until dark.
Step 3: Add blended peppers and cook until reduced.
Step 4: Season with salt.
Step 5: Serve beans topped with the pepper sauce.

recipes.title: Eba and Ogbono Soup

benefits: Ogbono seeds are rich in protein and healthy fats

instructions: Step 1: Boil meat with seasoning.
Step 2: Add palm oil and ogbono paste, stirring constantly.
Step 3: Simmer until thick and stretchy.
Step 4: Season to taste.
Step 5: Serve with eba (prepared from garri and hot water).

recipes.title: Tuwo Shinkafa

risks: High carb — not ideal for diabetics in large portions

instructions: Step 1: Boil rice until very soft.
Step 2: Mash with a wooden spoon until smooth.
Step 3: Shape into balls.
Step 4: Serve with soup (miyan kuka, miyan taushe, etc.).

recipes.title: Miyan Kuka

benefits: Baobab leaves are very high in calcium and iron
risks: Contains dried leaves — some may have been sun-dried in dusty conditions

instructions: Step 1: Boil beef with onions and seasoning until tender.
Step 2: Add ground crayfish and ginger.
Step 3: Sprinkle kuka powder into the pot while stirring.
Step 4: Simmer 10 minutes until thickened.
Step 5: Serve with tuwo shinkafa.

recipes.title: Chicken Suya Skewers
instructions: Step 1: Coat chicken in suya spice and oil.
Step 2: Skewer the chicken pieces.
Step 3: Grill until charred and cooked through.
Step 4: Serve with onions.

recipes.title: Waakye

benefits: Beans + rice combo provides complete protein
risks: Can be high in sodium if served with lots of salted fish

instructions: Step 1: Soak beans overnight.
Step 2: Boil beans until half-cooked.
Step 3: Add rice, onions, and sorghum leaves.
Step 4: Cook until rice and beans are tender.
Step 5: Serve with shito (pepper sauce) and fried plantain.

recipes.title: Fufu with Light Soup

benefits: Cassava and plantain are naturally gluten-free
risks: Cassava-based fufu is very dense — portion control matters

instructions: Step 1: Boil cassava and plantain; pound into fufu.
Step 2: In a separate pot, boil fish or goat with tomatoes, onions, and chili until tender.
Step 3: Simmer the soup until reduced and flavorful.
Step 4: Serve the soup hot with fufu.

recipes.title: Banku and Tilapia

benefits: Tilapia is high in protein and omega-3
Grilled fish is healthier than fried
risks: Banku is fermented — some may find it difficult to digest

instructions: Step 1: Mix corn and cassava dough; ferment 1-2 days.
Step 2: Cook, stirring constantly, until firm — this makes banku.
Step 3: Grill tilapia over charcoal until cooked.
Step 4: Blend tomatoes, onions, and chili for a dipping sauce.
Step 5: Serve hot.

recipes.title: Groundnut Soup

benefits: Groundnuts are rich in protein and healthy fats

instructions: Step 1: Boil chicken or fish until tender.
Step 2: Blend tomatoes, onion, and chili into a paste.
Step 3: Add groundnut paste to the pot; stir to combine.
Step 4: Simmer 20 minutes until the soup thickens.
Step 5: Serve with rice balls or fufu.

recipes.title: Red Red

benefits: Beans are high in fiber and plant protein
risks: Fried plantains are high in oil

instructions: Step 1: Boil beans until soft.
Step 2: Heat palm oil, fry onions and tomatoes.
Step 3: Add beans; simmer 10 min.
Step 4: Fry sliced plantains in oil until golden.
Step 5: Serve beans topped with plantains.

recipes.title: Thieboudienne

benefits: Very balanced dish — protein + carb + vegetables

instructions: Step 1: Stuff fish with a paste of parsley, garlic, and chili.
Step 2: Brown fish in oil; set aside.
Step 3: Sauté onions; add blended tomatoes and cook until thick.
Step 4: Add water and vegetables; simmer 20 minutes.
Step 5: Add rice and cook until tender.
Step 6: Serve with the fish on top.

recipes.title: Yassa Chicken

benefits: Onions and lemon add vitamin C
risks: Marinade may be high in salt
Fried chicken is higher in fat than grilled

instructions: Step 1: Marinate chicken with lemon juice, mustard, salt, and pepper for 30 min.
Step 2: Grill chicken until cooked; set aside.
Step 3: Sauté onions until soft and translucent.
Step 4: Add remaining marinade; simmer 10 min.
Step 5: Return chicken to pan and simmer 5 min.
Step 6: Serve with rice or bread.
